hints: Focus on what types of intermolecular forces each substance can have, not just the state change itself.
Remember that $\text{O}_2$ is a non-polar diatomic molecule, so it cannot have hydrogen bonding or permanent dipole-dipole forces.
Check both the force type and the direction of change, melting or boiling overcomes forces while freezing forms them.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the force means**

Great start, let's decode the wording. Temporary dipole-induced dipole forces are just another name for London (dispersion) forces.

They exist in all molecules, but the word *only* means the substance must have no hydrogen bonding and no permanent dipole-dipole forces.

**Sort the molecules by polarity**

Now look at each substance. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ both have O-H groups, so they hydrogen bond. $\text{O}_2$ is non-polar with an even sharing of electrons, so London forces only. $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$ is a non-polar hydrocarbon, so London forces only too.

**Check the direction of the change**

This is the clever part. Melting (s to l) and boiling (l to g) *overcome* forces by separating particles. Freezing (l to s) *forms* forces as particles come together.

$$\text{solid} \rightarrow \text{liquid} \rightarrow \text{gas: forces overcome}$$
$$\text{gas} \rightarrow \text{liquid} \rightarrow \text{solid: forces formed}$$

**Pick the match**

Only solid oxygen melting to liquid oxygen both has London forces only AND overcomes forces in that direction. That gives us our answer.

options.A: Incorrect. Liquid ethanol, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH(l)}$, has hydrogen bonding due to its O-H group, plus permanent dipole-dipole and London forces. Boiling to gas overcomes all of these, not only London forces.
options.B: Incorrect. Ice, $\text{H}_2\text{O(s)}$, is held together by extensive hydrogen bonding as well as London forces. Melting overcomes hydrogen bonds too, so it is not London forces only.
options.C: Correct. Oxygen, $\text{O}_2$, is a non-polar simple molecule with no hydrogen bonding and no permanent dipole. Solid to liquid overcomes only weak London (temporary dipole-induced dipole) forces between molecules.
options.D: Incorrect. This is a classic trap. Butane, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$, does have only London forces, but (l) to (s) is freezing. Freezing forms intermolecular forces as particles pack together, it does not overcome them.
